evidence.claim: 3Q26 10-Q: data center financing 'has generally become more difficult'; neoclouds, colocation providers and other tenants are increasingly viewed as high credit risks, which may cancel projects and push developers to negotiate lower equipment prices.
evidence.numbers: A Brookfield-affiliated financing vehicle was 26% of 3Q revenue and the largest receivable (31%); the supplier is carrying more of the working capital (contract assets $858.6mn).

evidence.claim: Meta backs two off-balance-sheet JV campuses (Louisiana/Hyperion, Texas/El Paso) with 4-year initial leases plus residual value guarantees. Partners and their lenders fund 80%, and the leases and guarantees of an AA- tenant carry the debt.
evidence.numbers: Max RVG $41.49bn at 30 Sep 2026 vs $28.09bn at YE25; total max exposure $68.40bn; development cost ~$27bn and ~$14bn.

evidence.claim: The tenant's own credit is drifting: Meta had negative free cash flow, moved to net debt, and created non-voting Class C stock for capital raising, among other purposes (also employee compensation, acquisitions, general corporate purposes). Management said it has no specific financing plans.
evidence.numbers: FCF -$2.12bn; cash and securities $82.45bn vs debt $83.67bn; capex $34.91bn = 106% of OCF.

evidence.claim: AMD agreed credit support for TensorWave's 222 MW lease at Fermi, a chip supplier standing behind a neocloud tenant.
Wells Fargo puts AWS- or Nvidia-backed data center bonds at about 6.8–7.2% and CoreWeave- or Oracle-backed at 8–9% or more.
Project debt backed by Google-supported and investment-grade leases priced at about 6.1–6.2%.
A facility backed by three-year contracts with weaker customers priced at SOFR + 550 bps and had to widen in syndication.
Phase II notes against an unbacked CoreWeave lease priced at 9.875%, the most expensive project debt among landlords.
A facility backed by one investment-grade customer priced at SOFR + 225 bps, rated A3.

question: Does the tenant's credit, not the asset, set what developers and neoclouds pay to borrow?
summary: Every 2026 financing points the same way. Debt backed by investment-grade contracts or a hyperscaler backstop prices near 6–7%; the same assets against weaker tenants pay 9–10% or more. October's selloff widened the gap.
title: Tenant credit sets the cost of capital
